newsitem.title: GERMANY: E.German wheat harvest to be medium-quality - ZMP.
newsitem.headline: E.German wheat harvest to be medium-quality - ZMP.

text.p: Eastern Germany is headed for a medium-quality wheat crop, according to early harvest reports published by the farm price and marketing office ZMP.

A higher area will bring larger volumes but the effects of spring drought and excessive rainfall in June/July have taken their toll on yields and baking qualities, a weekly report from ZMP's Berlin office showed.
The region last year accounted for 6.2 million tonnes out of Germany's 18.9-million tonne wheat crop.
This year, it expanded its combined winter, spring and durum wheat area to 977,369 hectares from 937,417 ha in 1996.

Protein counts in Mecklenburg, the second largest producer, were between 10 and 17 percent while Brandenburg, where the wheat area is the region's smallest, reported satisfactory Hagberg numbers and natural weights, ZMP wrote.
The harvest in the top producer state, Saxony-Anhalt, was 40-70 percent complete, with proteins sufficient but Hagbergs disappointing.
Thuringia, the number three, said the bulk of its harvest was of medium quality.
Saxony, the number four, gave an overall wheat yield range of 6.5-11.0 tonnes per hectare (tph).
Germany's national average winter wheat yield in 1996 was 7.32 tph.
ZMP said initial problems with low rye falling numbers were under control

Mecklenburg reported numbers between 100 and 170 seconds, with 120 generally agreed to be the minimum bread rye quality, while Thuringia said one third of its rye harvest was above 120 and another third even above 150.
Saxony said earlier problems with low falling numbers were being overcome while Brandenburg said yields were average, but did not comment on falling numbers.
Saxony-Anhalt appeared to be the only state with more severe problems -- 40 to 60 percent of its rye harvest looked set to be below 120 seconds.
